signal: STRUCTURAL FINDING (negative, re-evidenced 27/08/2026 with a wider window than the original run): there are effectively ZERO ATM or cash-automation tenders on the Slovenian portal javnih narocil. Sweeps re-run this date: CPV 30123200 'avtomatski stroji za izdajo bankovcev' (automatic banknote-dispensing machines = ATMs), including all subordinate codes, returns 0 notices since 01/01/2024; CPV 30123600 (coin-handling machines) plus subordinates returns 0 since 01/01/2024; CPV 30132000 / 30132200 / 30132300 (sorting equipment, banknote-handling) returns 6 notices since 01/01/2024, ALL of them Posta Slovenije PARCEL and LETTER sorters - not one banknote sorter; CPV 35121200 (counterfeit detection) returns 6 notices since 01/01/2024, ALL of them FURS desktop banknote counters ('JN 19/2025 BAN', 'JN 25/2025 BAN', 'JN 7/2025 PON') - no bank at all. Title wildcard '%bankomat%' returns just 2 notices in the portal's entire history, both from Mestna obcina Slovenj Gradec in 2019 subsidising the OPERATING COSTS of ATMs in the villages of Pamece and Podgorje - i.e. the only 'ATM' procurement Slovenia has ever published is a municipality paying to keep rural ATMs alive, never a bank buying machines. Title wildcard '%samopostrezn%' (self-service) returns 51 notices ever, of which the only ones since 2025 are Slovenske zeleznice railway ticket-machine maintenance. REASON: NLB, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, OTP banka, SKB, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka and Addiko are private companies and are NOT contracting authorities under ZJN-3 (the Slovenian public procurement act), and Bankart - the banks' shared card and payments processor - does not publish either. The only banking-sector contracting authorities in Slovenia are Banka Slovenije (central bank), SID banka (state development bank) and, as a utilities-sector buyer, Posta Slovenije.
